title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 36
paragraphs: Meanwhile the Delphians, having been informed of this, had been driven to extreme fear; and in their great terror they consulted the oracle about the sacred objects — whether they should bury them in the earth or carry them off to another land. But the god forbade them to meddle with these, saying that he was able by himself to take care of his own. On hearing this, they began to take thought for themselves: they sent their children and women across to Achaia on the other side of the sea, while most of the men themselves went up toward the summits of Parnassos and carried their property to the Corykian cave, and others took refuge at Amphissa of the Locrians. In short, the Delphians had all left the town except for sixty men and the prophet of the oracle.
